title: Beyond R²: Seasonal Effects, Residual Dependence, and Model Adequacy in Beijing PM2.5 Regression

slides.title: Beyond R²
slides.subtitle: Seasonal Effects, Residual Dependence, and Model Adequacy in Beijing PM2.5 Regression
slides.statement: What structure remains after adjusting for weather and season?
slides.notes: Introduce a statistical adequacy investigation using UCI observations. Weather is measured on the same day as the response: this is contemporaneous estimation, not an advance-forecast benchmark. The original confirmatory regressions are distinguished from exploratory work developed after the test year was viewed.

slides.title: Does season add information beyond weather?
cards: Do three seasonal terms add information after weather adjustment?
Does the conditional wind association differ by season?
Do residual patterns support the assumptions behind inference?
slides.notes: H1 compares M1 with M2; H2 compares M2 with M3. The third question concerns the errors, not another search for favorable p-values. Season can represent omitted processes, so seasonal coefficients describe conditional association rather than a causal mechanism.

slides.title: Daily data, chronological evaluation
lines: Wanliu selected by training completeness from 12 UCI stations.
Daily means: ≥18 valid hours; rainfall totals: 24 hours.
Also require 18 jointly observed core hours; preserve calendar gaps.
slides.notes: The source contains 420,768 hourly station records. Wanliu retains 1,441 of 1,461 calendar dates. Each mean uses its own valid hours; there is no target imputation or outcome-based trimming. Centers and quantile thresholds use training data only. Local time and rainfall-amount assumptions are documented in the report.

slides.title: Three nested multiple regressions
lines: Training-only centering · winter reference · original concentration scale
M2 wind: -49.0 µg/m³ per m/s, conditional on other weather and season.
slides.notes: Each added block has three parameters. In M3, seasonal offsets apply at the training mean wind speed and the base wind coefficient is the winter slope. Every design is full rank; conditioning is separate from statistical uncertainty. The wind coefficient is an observational association, not an intervention effect.

slides.title: Classical ANOVA and robust inference
lines: Neither primary joint hypothesis rejects at 5%.
Seven-calendar-day Bartlett HAC · joint χ²(3) Wald · two-test Holm family
slides.equation: F = (SSE reduction / added df) / full-model residual mean square
slides.notes: Classical F uses an iid, constant-variance Gaussian reference for exact calibration. HAC retains actual calendar separations and uses n/(n−p). Its Wald reference is asymptotic. The 14/30-day bandwidth checks are descriptive sensitivities. Failure to reject is not proof that seasonal structure is absent.

slides.title: Residual dependence remains
slides.caption: M3 training R² 0.221 · lag-one residual r 0.512 · 719 adjacent-date pairs
slides.notes: The first-lag correlation is substantial after weather and season adjustment. Missing calendar positions are retained and pair counts vary by lag. Daily aggregation has not made the errors independent. Read the magnitude and pattern rather than treating an auxiliary p-value as an independence certificate.

slides.title: Residual spread and distributional shape
slides.caption: Training M3 · unequal spread and upper-tail departure · no flagged day deleted
slides.notes: The scatter and Q–Q plot address different aspects of adequacy. The Q–Q plot does not test independence. Serial, Koenker/Breusch–Pagan and influence diagnostics have calibration assumptions under dependence. Forty M3 observations exceed the Cook's-distance screening guide, which does not establish that they are errors.

slides.title: Average gain, high-day failure
slides.caption: µg/m³ · 357 test days · 17 high days · 3 negative estimates retained
slides.notes: The fixed validation rule chooses M3, with M2 only 1.11% above the minimum. Overall signed error is positive, but high-day error is strongly negative. The high-day cutoff is 234.655 µg/m³, learned from training. There is no clipping or test-year refit; dependent errors preclude a naive independent-day interval for performance differences.

slides.title: Exploratory temporal and weather extensions
slides.caption: 721 train / 354 validation / 355 test · M3 refit on the common sample
slides.notes: The five candidates share dates. Extra weather is dew point and two wind-vector components; the lag is the previous calendar day's observed PM2.5. Log estimates use a training-only smearing factor times exp(linear predictor), minus one. This does not guarantee nonnegativity. The viewed test year supplies descriptive comparisons, not independent confirmation.

slides.title: AR(1) sensitivity to five short gaps
lines: Paired likelihood fits change only row versus calendar spacing.
Transitions use ρᵈ with gap-adjusted innovation variance.
Nominal decisions agree; estimated-ρ uncertainty remains approximate.
slides.notes: Original GLSAR compresses rows across five two-day training gaps. The paired check holds estimation and first-observation treatment fixed. A separate dense covariance verifies wind coefficients and profile objectives. Nominal H1/H2 conclusions remain unchanged, including within-method Holm adjustment. This does not validate stationary Gaussian AR(1) or override the primary HAC/Holm result.

slides.title: Cross-station consistency
slides.caption: Within-station Holm: H1 6/12, H2 2/12 · not a full 24-test correction
slides.notes: Each station has its own eligible dates, centers and cutoff. All M2 wind intervals lie below zero. Seasonal findings vary; M3 beats the training-mean baseline at 11/12 sites, except Gucheng. Shared pollution and weather make these dependent sites, not independent replications.

slides.title: High recall brings many false alarms
slides.caption: High day: PM2.5 ≥234.655 µg/m³ (training 95th percentile) · 17 test high days · not a health standard
slides.notes: The concentration threshold is the training daily 95th percentile. Validation F1 selects the probability cutoff, breaking ties toward a higher value; test labels do not select it. A 0.5 cutoff detects none. AUC describes ranking, while this table shows the selected cutoff's burden. Rare, dependent events limit precision; odds-ratio intervals assume independence.

slides.title: Two groups of training pollutant profiles
slides.caption: Pollutant-specific eligible dates · new-period cluster stability untested
slides.notes: The existing verified heatmap displays the standardized training profiles and cluster labels. The largest merge-height gap for k=2…5 chooses two groups. The lower mean-PM2.5 group contains Changping, Dingling, Huairou, Shunyi. Group labels describe this period; they do not identify validated geographic or risk classes.

slides.title: Limits of the evidence
cards: One city, four historical years; missingness and omitted drivers can affect associations.
Residual dependence remains; individual intervals and station-wise tests are not simultaneous protection.
Observed same-day weather and a reused exploratory test year limit claims about future prediction.
slides.notes: Mention spatially matched weather, emissions/transport and boundary-layer information. HAC cannot repair an inadequate conditional mean. A common smearing factor can miss varying conditional error distributions. Cross-station consistency and separate implementation checks do not establish causal effects or independent scientific replication.

slides.title: Model adequacy requires more than explained variance
lines: Seasonal terms reduce SSE; adjusted joint evidence is insufficient at 5%.
M3 lowers average error while retaining serial structure and high-day failure.
Next: an unseen period, prespecified rules and explicit covariate availability.
slides.notes: Return to the question: fit reduction, inference and error behavior must be considered together. Smaller errors for exploratory temporal/weather models motivate further study without confirming them. A new evaluation should define the information available when an estimate is issued and avoid retuning on the current test year.
